newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market was liquid on Thursday with short-term trading rates quoted softer, dealers said.

They said the central Reserve Bank had auctioned Z$400 million worth of treasury bills at 16.47 percent to mop up excess liquidity. Discount houses were re-selling the central bank paper on the secondary market at 16.40 percent, unchanged from the previous day.

Rates for NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 17.50 and 17.40 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 19 and 18 percent while bankers acceptance bills were being bought at 16.50 percent, down from 17.75 and at 16.40 from 17 percent. Call money slipped to 16 percent from 18.50 percent.
Figures from the Reserve Bank showed the market closed with a slight Z$29.6 million shortage on Wednesday, an improvement over a deficit of Z$138 million on Tuesday.
